summary.oneLiner: A clean, broad-based beat: PAT +37% YoY to ₹796cr on core PPOP +41%, NIM up 47bps YoY to 5.9%, credit cost halved to 0.8% and ROA/ROE at 1.7%/15.6% — with loan growth (23%) and deposit growth (24%) both running well ahead of the private-bank system (17%/14%). The strategic story this quarter is that the unsecured cycle has turned (slippages -22% YoY, MFI +5% QoQ, PL +19% QoQ) just as the bank's newer geographies and newer products (gold +130% YoY, renewable-energy financing +120% YoY) start contributing — leaving management ~10bps short of its stated 1.8% ROA target and unusually relaxed about the pending ECL transition.

one-line thesis: A clean, broad-based beat: PAT +37% YoY to ₹796cr on core PPOP +41%, NIM up 47bps YoY to 5.9%, credit cost halved to 0.8% and ROA/ROE at 1.7%/15.6% — with loan growth (23%) and deposit growth (24%) both running well ahead of the private-bank system (17%/14%). The strategic story this quarter is that the unsecured cycle has turned (slippages -22% YoY, MFI +5% QoQ, PL +19% QoQ) just as the bank's newer geographies and newer products (gold +130% YoY, renewable-energy financing +120% YoY) start contributing — leaving management ~10bps short of its stated 1.8% ROA target and unusually relaxed about the pending ECL transition.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs called out: PAT includes an additional one-time provision of ₹23cr from tightening NPA-provisioning norms in selected products — described by Vivek Tripathi as pure alignment ("It was just a more of a alignment of all unsecured products, be it credit card, MFI, and PL on the same lines"), not a new stress signal. Also note the QoQ NIM decline (-7bps) is seasonal-benefit reversal, and the QoQ provisions jump (+38%) is seasonal — Q4 is structurally the bank's strongest quarter, so management explicitly instructed analysts to compare YoY, not QoQ.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Loan/franchise growth: compound at 2.0-2.5x India's nominal GDP growth — framed as a 10-year run-rate, not a one-year number.

ROA: stated target 1.8% (currently 1.7%). Management explicitly declined a NIM guide; the ~10bps bridge is to come from opex and credit cost improving vs full-FY26, plus a recovery in other income "in the next 6 to 9 months."
Margin: no NIM guidance given. Directional: cost of funds has bottomed out, will be "stable to maybe increasing a little bit"; asset yields will reflect mix.
Cost-to-assets: guided to improve on a full-year basis vs the 4.0% Q1 print, as operating leverage plays out.
Distribution: 100+ additional deposit branches to be added this year (16 added in Q1).
ECL transition: management expects the impact to be neutral given low historical LGDs/PDs and existing Stage-3 provisioning cushion; refuses to quantify now, promises "some colors by end of Q3."

MFI/inclusive banking: book capped at up to 10% of the total loan book (PSL/small-and-marginal-farmer obligation driven, not an ROA driver). Steady-state MFI credit cost re-rated from the old 3% assumption to ~2.5% now that the CGFMU guarantee cost replaces buffer-building.
CGFMU claims: claims on the crystallised FY26 NPA pool to be lodged by end-Q2 FY27 and realised by mid-to-end December 2026.
FCNR: no specific mobilisation target — deliberately declined ("we are not targeting now a specific one because if you don't have a leverage, it's difficult to convince the customer").
order book & pipeline: Not applicable in the conventional sense (bank). Pipeline proxies: disbursements +42% YoY in a seasonally soft quarter; new CASA acquisition with 80% YoY growth in premium accounts; >1 lakh new credit cards issued in Q1; gold-loan product extended to 400+ additional branches taking distribution to 1,300+ branches; pre-approved PL offers up >3x from propensity models.
segment / subsidiary detail: Retail secured (67% of loan book): +23% YoY, +4% QoQ.
Wheels: ₹48,600cr, +28% YoY, +5% QoQ — new-vehicle demand strong, traction in newer geographies (South, UP, East).
Gold loans: ₹4,500cr, +130% YoY, +15% QoQ — Fincare-inherited capability scaled into AU's North-West distribution; >80% rural, avg ticket ~₹2.5 lakh (majority <₹5 lakh), portfolio IRR ~15.5%.
Mortgages (micro-business loans + affordable housing): +12% YoY, +2% QoQ — the laggard, but disbursements +28% YoY, i.e. the book is inflecting.

Commercial banking: ₹32,800cr, +34% YoY, +6% QoQ, broad-based across sub-verticals; strategy is to make it progressively self-funded via current accounts + transaction banking/CMS/trade. Renewable-energy book +120%+ YoY — lending to PM-KUSUM Component A/C developers, typical project 2-5MW, concentrated in Rajasthan then Gujarat/Maharashtra/MP; attraction is favourable PPAs plus capital subsidy improving project viability. SME/business-banking book drove the small QoQ uptick in commercial-banking NPAs (seasonal Q1 pattern).
Inclusive banking (MFI): +15% YoY, +5% QoQ; collection efficiency 99.5% (only ~20bps below Q4, vs a normally seasonal Q1 dip); 96% of the book covered by CGFMU guarantee.

Digital unsecured: +3% YoY, +7% QoQ. Personal loans +24% YoY, +19% QoQ off a low base — 100% cross-sell to existing bank customers (99% ETB), scorecard/analytics-driven; credit card marginal growth, still loss-making, PL at/around breakeven.

Liabilities, four verticals: branch banking 60% of deposits; government & interbank 21%; commercial banking & wholesale 7%; FIG 8%. New zero-forex-margin/zero-charge international retail remittance product launched (claimed a first among Indian private banks).
growth verticals / optionality: Gold loans (₹4,500cr, +130%), renewable-energy project finance (+120%), transaction banking/forex (income +46% YoY) and the re-started personal-loan/credit-card engines are the four optionality legs. The structural one is geography: the bank was a North-West franchise until ~2 years ago and — post-Fincare and via deeper UP/Bihar/East/South buildout — now describes itself as pan-India, with the explicit claim that a full-India franchise is what makes the 2-2.5x-nominal-GDP compounding credible for a decade.
6a. moat & competitive position: CGFMU guarantee coverage on 96% of the MFI book structurally converts a volatile credit-cost line into a predictable premium: "instead of building up the buffers, we are securing protection on that book" (Gaurav Jain) — this is why the steady-state MFI credit-cost assumption drops from 3% to ~2.5% with far lower variance.

Low LGDs on a 67%-secured retail book, which management leans on as the reason the ECL transition should be P&L-neutral: "our retail secured asset and even on the commercial side, it's largely secured. Our LGDs are pretty low compared to what the industry would look like."
Cross-sell moat on the liability base — the entire restarted PL book is sourced from existing (99% ETB) customers with transaction-scorecard underwriting, i.e. growth without new-to-bank risk.

Fincare-acquired capability (gold-loan operating ecosystem: valuers, ops, origination + an experienced MFI team) is being redeployed into AU's own distribution — a genuine acquisition synergy rather than balance-sheet addition.
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 5.9%, +47bps YoY but -7bps QoQ; cost of funds flat at 6.48% as higher SA/wholesale costs offset residual retail-TD repricing. Management says cost of funds has bottomed, so NIM defence now depends on asset mix, not liability repricing.
Credit cost (incl. CGFMU fee) 0.8% vs 1.4% — the single largest driver of ROA improvement.

Cost-to-assets 4.0% ex-CGFMU (vs 3.9%); opex +26% YoY but -1% QoQ, and headcount actually declined in May — the first monthly decline — attributed to AI absorbing back-office (operations, accounts, finance) work while front-line hiring continues.

Product-level profitability disclosure declined: credit card explicitly loss-making, PL "around breakeven" — management asked for time before being held to product ROAs. Credit-card yield is subdued because the revolve share fell after underwriting tightening ~18 months ago.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): 100+ new deposit branches planned for the year (16 in Q1) — the main physical-expansion commitment to track.
Gold loan rolled out to 400+ more branches in Q1, now 1,300+ branches distributing the product.

Technology: agentic-AI gold-loan origination platform live in controlled/mobile-native mode, to be extended to branches in a "calibrated manner"; mortgage origination to be built on the same platform; AI transformation underway across vehicle finance, PL and credit cards; commercial-banking journey on a new platform; unified lead-management platform launched; Customer-360 live; AI voice bots across 11 languages; AI auto-resolving 70% of AML alerts; >90% of transactions/service requests on the AU 0101 app.
capital allocation: No dividend/buyback/raise discussed. Capital is being deployed into (a) distribution — 100+ branches, (b) technology ~₹1,000cr p.a., and (c) balance-sheet growth at 2-2.5x nominal GDP. Funding-side allocation choices: within bulk deposits the bias is toward non-callable TDs (stable deposits 79% of total), and FCNR rates were raised to ~7.4-7.5% opportunistically rather than to a target. On the CD ratio, Sanjay Agarwal explicitly refused to treat it as an optimisation variable: "CD ratio ex-refinance is ~80%. So we don't look this number to optimize anything."
risks & watch-items: ECL transition is un-quantified. Every other large bank is putting a number on transition and steady-state credit-cost impact; AU declined twice, saying models are preliminary and the outcome depends on Board-approved accelerated-provisioning and write-off policies. Their claim of neutrality rests on the Stage-3 cushion covering Stage-1/2 build. Deferred to end-Q3 — a hard date to hold them to.

NIM has no guidance and cost of funds has bottomed. With savings and wholesale rates already raised and the mix shifting toward lower-yield secured/gold assets, the ROA bridge to 1.8% now depends entirely on opex leverage, credit cost and a hoped-for other-income recovery — three soft levers.

Unsecured recovery is early and low-base. PL +19% QoQ and MFI +5% QoQ are off depressed bases; credit card is still loss-making. Management refused to give unsecured growth targets ("industry has just started to revive after almost six to eight quarters of degrowth").
Commercial banking NPA uptick QoQ in the SME/business-banking book — described as a normal Q1 seasonal pattern that "slows down" later; worth verifying in Q2.
NSFR structurally lower than pre-2024 (108-109 vs 115-120+ historically) — management's answer was simply "that's the range we operate," with no explanation of why the range reset.

MFI is deliberately not an ROA engine — capped at 10% of book and run for PSL/small-and-marginal-farmer obligation. Growth there is compliance-driven, so it should not be extrapolated as a profit lever.
Succession is now an explicit board project. Sanjay Agarwal spoke unprompted about not having "infinite years" — constructive, but it is a governance transition to monitor.
management quality / tone: Confident, specific and notably willing to say "no." Gaurav Jain refused to give NIM guidance and corrected an analyst who inferred one ("we haven't guided for stable, there's no guidance on NIM"); Vivek Tripathi twice declined to quantify ECL rather than offering a soft number; Prince Tiwari pushed back on judging credit-card/PL risk-adjusted yields at this stage and conceded plainly that credit cards are loss-making. Sanjay Agarwal was candid on the ROA gap ("we are just looking a 10 bps from here… it's not that big difference from our stated target") and unusually open on leadership succession, framing the elevation of Yogesh Jain as deliberate, unhurried institution-building rather than a reaction. The overall register is a bank that believes it is past its unsecured credit cycle and is now selling durability rather than a growth story.
non-obvious takeaways: Headcount fell month-on-month for the first time (April→May) because of AI, not a hiring freeze — and management linked it to a second-order effect that matters for cost structure: banking roles that previously could not be remote can now be done "from home or anywhere." A cost-to-assets improvement driven by structural back-office automation is a very different quality of operating leverage than one driven by growth outpacing fixed costs.

The MFI business model has changed shape, not just improved. Buffer-building has been replaced by a paid guarantee (CGFMU on 96% of the book), so the credit-cost line is now a premium expense with far less variance — the reported credit-cost improvement is partly a form change, and Sanjay Agarwal was explicit that economically "it's a similar thing. You pay credit cost now. Guarantee cost now."

Renewable-energy lending is a quiet, policy-driven niche built over three years inside commercial banking — PM-KUSUM Component A/C, 2-5MW developer projects — where the credit case rests on the capital subsidy plus attractive discom PPAs, not on the renewable theme itself.

CGFMU coverage on GNPA is materially lower than on the live book (96%) because a chunk of current NPAs originate from vintage, pre-coverage pools — so the guarantee provides less protection against already-recognised stress than the headline suggests.

The one externally-mappable item is PM-KUSUM solar developer financing.

hero.oneLiner: A clean, broad-based beat: PAT +37% YoY to ₹796cr on core PPOP +41%, NIM up 47bps YoY to 5.9%, credit cost halved to 0.8% and ROA/ROE at 1.7%/15.6% — with loan growth (23%) and deposit growth (24%) both running well ahead of the private-bank system (17%/14%). The strategic story this quarter is that the unsecured cycle has turned (slippages -22% YoY, MFI +5% QoQ, PL +19% QoQ) just as the bank's newer geographies and newer products (gold +130% YoY, renewable-energy financing +120% YoY) start contributing — leaving management ~10bps short of its stated 1.8% ROA target and unusually relaxed about the pending ECL transition.
